body.heading: Where in the world is Guinea-Bissau?
paragraphs: Guinea-Bissau is a country in Western Africa, which is part of Africa.

body.heading: The capital city
paragraphs: The capital of Guinea-Bissau is Bissau.

body.heading: Words you might hear
paragraphs: People in Guinea-Bissau speak Crioulo and Portuguese. Crioulo, a language that grew out of Portuguese, is the one most people speak; Portuguese is the official language.

body.heading: Money in your pocket
paragraphs: The money of Guinea-Bissau is the West African CFA franc. The CFA franc is shared with neighbouring countries, so the same money works across the region.

body.heading: How big is Guinea-Bissau?
paragraphs: Guinea-Bissau covers about 36,000 square kilometres of land and inland water. That makes it about half the size of Sierra Leone.

body.heading: Two places we'd love to visit
paragraphs: Orango, in the Bijagós Archipelago, is famous for saltwater hippos that swim in the sea, plus sacred forests and giant sea turtles nesting on its beaches.
Bolama was the first capital, and its wide, quiet avenues of faded grand buildings under mango trees feel like a town from a storybook.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Find Guinea-Bissau on a map or globe. Which continent is it on — and can you name a country that sits next to it?
2. Spark and Mango can visit only ONE of the two places in this article. Which should they choose — and what would you pack for the trip?
